subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should managed Gateway installs ship the fixed 8192 MB heap default from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96250 now, or require a first-class tunable heap surface before resolving this issue?
rationale: Current main still has the reported failure mode, but choosing a fixed startup default versus a configurable knob is an operator-impact and low-memory-host policy decision.

options.title: Land fixed emergency default
options.body: Accept the open PR's generated 8192 MB heap-only default now and track any durable tuning surface separately.

options.title: Require tunable surface first
options.body: Pause the open PR until maintainers choose and validate a CLI/config/env heap-size surface with upgrade proof.

options.title: Reject daemon heap mitigation
options.body: Keep daemon startup unchanged and rely on state-size fixes or manual wrappers, leaving this issue open only for memory-root-cause work.

recommendation.title: Land fixed emergency default
recommendation.body: Accept the open PR's generated 8192 MB heap-only default now and track any durable tuning surface separately.

likelyOwner.reason: The daemon service environment history points to steipete as the strongest current routing candidate for install/default policy.
